🔥 visual-explainer | HTML
🎯 Primary Use Case: To enhance the readability and visual presentation of information generated by coding agents, converting raw terminal output into accessible and interactive HTML pages.
✨ Key Features: • Generates styled HTML pages from terminal output • Supports diagrams, diff reviews, plan audits, data tables, and project recaps • Interactive Mermaid diagrams with zoom and pan • Dark/light themes • No build step or dependencies beyond a browser for basic use
📖 Summary: Visual-explainer is an agent skill that transforms complex terminal output, such as diagrams and tables, into user-friendly, styled HTML pages. It aims to make information generated by coding agents more readable and visually appealing, moving beyond basic ASCII art.
🔗 Links: • View Project ================ 🔓 Open Source

🔥 editor | TypeScript
🎯 Primary Use Case: To provide a flexible and extensible platform for creating and editing 3D architectural models, with a focus on local-first operation and seamless integration with AI agents for enhanced workflows.
✨ Key Features: • Open-source 3D architectural editor • Local-first architecture • Browser and CLI interface • React Three Fiber and WebGPU powered • AI agent integration via MCP
📖 Summary: Pascal Editor is an open-source, local-first 3D architectural editor that runs in the browser or via a CLI. It leverages React Three Fiber and WebGPU for its rendering capabilities and integrates with AI agents through the Model Context Protocol (MCP).
🔗 Links: • View Project • Homepage ================ 🔓 Open Source

🔥 OpenContext | JavaScript
🎯 Primary Use Case: To provide AI agents with a persistent memory and knowledge base, enabling them to retain context across different coding sessions, projects, and interactions, thereby improving efficiency and reducing repetition.
✨ Key Features: • Persistent memory for AI agents • Reuses existing coding agent CLIs (Codex/Claude/OpenCode) • Built-in Skills/tools for context management
📖 Summary: OpenContext is a personal context and knowledge store for AI agents, allowing them to maintain memory across sessions and projects. It integrates with existing coding agent CLIs (like Codex, Claude/OpenCode) and provides a GUI, skills, and tools to capture, search, and reuse project knowledge.
🔗 Links: • View Project • Homepage ================ 🔓 Open Source

✨ Text-Grab | C#
🎯 Primary Use Case: Extracting and copying text from any visible content on a Windows screen, especially from sources where text selection is not possible.
✨ Key Features: • OCR text extraction from various sources (screenshots, files) • Local and private processing (no internet required) • Multiple capture modes (Full-Screen, Window, Region, File) • Post-grab cleanup and editing tools • Clipboard output and direct editor integration
📖 Summary: Text Grab is a Windows application that uses Optical Character Recognition (OCR) to extract text from images, PDFs, and other on-screen content. It offers multiple capture modes, local processing for privacy, and integration options for seamless workflow integration.
🔗 Links: • View Project • Homepage ================ 🔓 Open Source

🔥 PageLM | TypeScript
🎯 Primary Use Case: To convert static study materials into dynamic, interactive learning tools using AI, making studying more engaging and effective.
✨ Key Features: • AI-powered transformation of study materials • Generates quizzes, flashcards, notes, and podcasts • Community-driven open-source project • Inspired by NotebookLM • Built with TypeScript, React, Node.js, and LangChain
📖 Summary: PageLM is an open-source AI-powered education platform that transforms study materials like PDFs and lecture notes into interactive learning resources. It aims to provide a community-driven alternative to tools like NotebookLM, offering features such as quizzes, flashcards, notes, and podcasts.
🔗 Links: • View Project ================ 🔓 Open Source

🚀 happy | TypeScript
🎯 Primary Use Case: Enables users to access and control AI coding assistants like Claude Code and Codex from any device (mobile, web, desktop) with enhanced security and convenience.
✨ Key Features: • Mobile and Web client for Claude Code and Codex • Realtime voice capabilities • End-to-end encryption • Seamless device switching (phone/desktop) • Push notifications
📖 Summary: Happy is a cross-platform client for AI coding assistants like Claude Code and Codex, offering mobile and web access with end-to-end encryption. It allows users to interact with their AI from anywhere, seamlessly switching between devices.
🔗 Links: • View Project • Homepage ================ 🔓 Open Source
